summary: The Data Center Coalition comments on PJM's July 31 Reliability Backstop Procurement proposal. It supports acceptance as a limited, one-time backstop and asks FERC to protect bilateral procurement, assign costs to the large loads driving the need, and keep new capacity on schedule.
ask: Accept PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement filing as a limited, one-time measure, consistent with the Coalition's principles on bilateral offsets, cost causation and getting infrastructure built.

points.point: The Coalition supports the backstop as a one-time measure and wants bilateral procurement kept as the preferred path.
points.quote: DCC supports moving forward with the RBP as a limited, one-time backstop.

points.point: PJM should not procure duplicative capacity for a customer that has arranged qualifying new capacity.
points.quote: Where a customer has arranged for qualifying new capacity to serve its incremental demand, PJM should not procure duplicative capacity on that customer’s behalf.

points.point: PJM proposes about 6.8 GW of new capacity under commitments of up to fifteen years.
points.quote: PJM proposes to procure approximately 6.8 GW of new capacity through commitments that may extend for as long as fifteen years.

points.point: Costs of serving new large loads should fall on the new large loads, not existing customers.
points.quote: should be borne by new large loads contributing to resource inadequacy and should not be shifted to existing residential, commercial, or industrial customers

points.point: DCC and the Virginia State Corporation Commission agreed to develop model retail tariff provisions for backstop costs.
points.quote: DCC and the Virginia State Corporation Commission have agreed to work together to develop model retail tariff provisions designed to appropriately assign RBP costs

points.point: Success is measured by megawatts reaching commercial operation, which depends on interconnection and transmission upgrades.
points.quote: measure of success should not be how many MW PJM contracts for, but how many MW actually reach commercial operation in time to address the identified reliability need.

throughLine.text: Comments in PJM's backstop docket ER26-3380. Its bring-your-own-capacity offsets and cost-causation principle bear on the E-7 adequacy report and on who pays for new load.

figures.label: PJM backstop procurement target
figures.quote: PJM proposes to procure approximately 6.8 GW of new capacity
